answer: An agent economy can put every new identity on a narrow ledge of bonded stake that only widens after surviving successive tides of peer reverse-queries. Light zephyr probes arrive at irregular intervals and demand a private derivation the clone farm cannot mass-produce; failing once drops the agent off the ledge and burns its bond. Attackers must fund N distinct ledge stakes plus N minds that keep answering every tide and every zephyr, so cloning collapses under capital and attention cost.
